1.why: All ten screens are static, flat panels with no animations, carousels, banners or pop-ups; only a persistent step bar, a form card, a collapsed help panel and a log panel.

2.why: The page heading, the blue-highlighted 'Next step:' callout and the single filled blue primary button clearly dominate each screen, though the dark 'Activity logs' block draws unnecessary visual weight.

3.why: Each screen carries exactly one task, one input group and one primary action, plus an explicit next-step instruction, so the required item is easy to locate; only the technical log block adds noise.

4.why: The numbered 8-step progress bar, per-screen 'Next step' reminders and on-screen display of the codes (864200, 246810, the recovery hash) remove most memory load, but she must still carry the new password and the 12–128 character policy across to the sign-in screen.

5.why: No 'remember me' checkbox, password-manager hint, show-password toggle or autofill affordance appears on the password or sign-in screens; the only autofill-like control is the task-specific 'Fill recovery code field' button.

6.why: The sign-in screen pre-fills the familiar email helena@hospital.test and the step chips stay recognizable, but there are no saved-device, saved-credential or previously-used-item indicators.

7.why: Text is short single-sentence prose in plain language with large readable type and high contrast, e.g. 'This is a calm, step-by-step process. You can stop and return later.'

8.why: No error state is shown in any of the ten screenshots; only the up-front password policy and generic notices are visible, so error-plus-remedy messaging cannot be confirmed.

9.why: Concrete examples are given for the codes (the mock code 246810 and the recovery string are displayed verbatim, with a 'Fill recovery code field' helper) and the password policy is spelled out, though no sample password is shown.

10.why: Only one authentication path exists — password plus emailed one-time code; there is no face, biometric or passkey choice presented, so the statement about clear alternative login choices does not hold.

11.why: Each screen offers one primary button and at most one secondary link (e.g. 'Use a different email address', 'Reset password instead'), so choice load is minimal.

12.why: Outcomes are explicitly stated, e.g. the green 'Password saved. Your new password is ready to use.' and 'Appointment request confirmed', reinforced by the highlighted step chip and the activity log.

13.why: A collapsible 'Help and safe authentication' panel appears on every screen alongside per-step tips and a repeated safety reminder, though the help content itself is hidden until expanded.

14.why: Recovery/back links exist ('Use a different email address', 'Return to sign in', 'Reset password instead', 'Return to account recovery start') and there are no timeouts, but no retry or edit affordance is visible on the password or code-entry screens.

15.why: Every screen uses the identical header, 8-step chip bar, white card with heading plus blue 'Next step' callout, blue primary button, safety reminder, help panel, log panel and 'No time limit' footer.
